checked.evidence: Decision 17 June 2020, EUR 15,000; loss of archived insurance contract deprived customer of access; failure to notify within 72 hours (Art. 33).

checked.evidence: s. 19: appointed by the Council of Ministers; qualifications of a Supreme Court judge; six-year term renewable once; dismissal only for mental or physical incapacity. 'On the proposal of the Minister' not specifically checked.

checked.claim: Commissioner imposes fines under s. 32(1); unpaid fines recovered as civil debt (s. 32(2))

checked.claim: Public bodies fineable, capped at EUR 200,000 for non-profit activities (s. 32(3)); EUR 46,500 fine on State Health Services Organisation
checked.evidence: s. 32: fine on a public authority or body ... 'may not exceed EUR 200,000'. The EUR 46,500 item could not be checked (DataGuidance page returned no article text); it is already flagged as unverified in the file.

checked.claim: s. 33 offences: 3 years/EUR 30,000; 1 year/EUR 10,000; 5 years/EUR 50,000 for national security
checked.evidence: s. 33: up to 3 years or EUR 30,000 or both; up to 1 year or EUR 10,000 or both for other listed offences; up to 5 years or EUR 50,000 where state interests are affected. Chief executive liability not checked.

checked.claim: Commissioner must inform complainant within 30 days of progress or outcome
checked.evidence: s. 24: examines the complaint and, 'where possible', informs the complainant in writing of its progress and outcome within 30 days. The 30 days is qualified, not absolute.
checked.replacement: Section 24 requires the Commissioner to examine complaints and, where possible, inform the complainant in writing of the progress or outcome within 30 days; the Commissioner may decline to examine a complaint for public-interest reasons. No time limit for complaining found.

checked.claim: Administrative Court, s. 28, recourse under Art. 146 of the Constitution
checked.evidence: s. 28: every natural or legal person has a right of recourse against a decision of the Commissioner before the Administrative Court.

checked.claim: 75 days under Art. 146(3) of the Constitution
checked.evidence: Not in the fetched sources. It matches the general constitutional rule (Art. 146(3), 75 days) as far as I know, and the file already flags it as a general rule.

checked.claim: No automatic suspension; provisional order needed
checked.evidence: No source fetched addresses this. Consistent with general Cypriot administrative law as far as I know.

checked.evidence: Rule of Law Report 2023: Court of Appeal created 'to deal with appeals against all judgments issued at first instance', with an administrative division; Supreme Constitutional Court and Supreme Court at third instance.
